title: Stealth priming and orchestrated rollback broker for VPC data-plane upgrades
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Private (VPC) data-plane runtime upgrades currently rely on blunt traffic shifts and coarse health probes, which cause short availability windows or require manual rollback coordination when KV caches and primed state diverge. Goal: implement a stealth priming and rollback broker that automates read-only warm-up, quorum-based health gating, and a reversible cutover path so we can perform major data-plane/runtime rollouts with near-zero customer-visible disruption.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade flow can promote a new runtime version for a tenant slice without any 5xx customer errors in production during cutover (verified by golden-traffic replay)
Automatic rollback triggers within 2 minutes for any of: >20% p95 latency regression, >5% error rate increase, KV hit-rate drop >30%, or failed golden-response checksum mismatch
Terraform/IaC plan hooks expose a preflight priming stage and a post-plan rollback token; plans must be idempotent and safe to re-run
Synthetic prewarm probes exercise model startup and KV cache replay with observable metrics surfaced in Console per-tenant dashboard
Rollback completes to original runtime in under 5 minutes with KV reconciliation and no manual DB migration steps
implementation_notes: Introduce a broker service (stateless API) that coordinates staged promotion and rollback tokens; broker persists small per-slice state in managed PostgreSQL with tenancy metadata
Extend Terraform modules with two new lifecycle hooks: preflight_terraform_priming (execs a priming job) and post_apply_rollback_token (outputs reversible token to SSM/Secrets manager)
Stealth priming: spin up new runtime replicas in read-only mode behind a shadow router that mirrors 1-2% of golden traffic for warm cache population without affecting production observability
Health gating: use quorum of synthetic probes + KV hit-rate + tail-latency to decide promotion; gates calculated per-slice and aggregated by broker
Rollback broker supports reverse-priming to resume traffic to previous runtime and perform state reconciliation (KV snapshot replay + cache diff) before full cutback
Make use of existing prewarm and priming libraries from ENG-21345 and integrate synthetic probes from ENG-41022 (references in dependencies)
rollout_steps: 1) Terraform plan with preflight hook: validates resource diffs and triggers prewarm job (no traffic change)
2) Broker creates candidate slice and attaches stealth shadow router; candidate replicas started in read-only mode
3) Mirror golden traffic at 1-2% through the shadow router; run KV cache-population and autoreplay for priming windows
4) Run synthetic golden-response checks and compare checksums against baseline responses
5) If health gates pass, broker issues timed promotion token and shifts progressive traffic (canary -> ramp) using slot-aware shaping
6) Monitor metrics for 10 minutes at each ramp step; if any threshold breaches, broker triggers rollback token
7) On success, broker marks candidate as primary and emits completed rollout event to audit logs and Console
rollback_playbook: Immediate automated rollback triggers on health breach: broker issues rollback token to Terraform orchestration and reverse-priming agent
Reverse-priming agent marks candidate as read-only, resumes mirrored traffic to previous primary, and performs KV reconciliation by applying snapshot diffs
If reconciliation fails, broker quarantines the candidate slice and drains traffic entirely to primary until manual investigation
Emit detailed rollback report to Slack incident channel, include terraform plan output, candidate logs (last 30m), and synthetic probe traces
Post-rollback: run a staged replay to identify root-cause (kernel/quantization mismatch, cache eviction pattern) and create an RCA ticket
testing_plan: Unit tests for broker token lifecycle and idempotency
Integration tests in staging that exercise Terraform preflight hooks with mocked priming jobs
Canary runs in staging using production-size slices (small cohort) and golden-traffic replay
Chaos test: simulate transient KV-store latency and confirm rollback triggers and reverse-priming correctness
Regression harness: run previous failing upgrade scenario from ENG-84672 and confirm no customer impact
metrics_and_alerts: metric: runtime.request_success_rate (threshold: drop > 5% over 2m triggers alert)
metric: runtime.p95_latency_ms (threshold: increase > 20% from baseline for 5m)
alerting: rollbroker.rollback_triggered (annotated with reason and slice id)
SLO burn: if error budget burn rate > 2x expected during rollout, escalate to emergency channel
